message.content:
**Your “Paris Dream Trip” – A 7‑Day Itinerary**

> *Assumptions:*  
> • You’ll arrive on **Monday morning** and depart Friday evening.  
> • Budget range: €1 200–€2 000 total (flight + stay + food & extras).  
> • Interests: art/history, gastronomy, leisurely strolls, iconic landmarks.  

Feel free to tweak the schedule—just let me know what you’d like more/less of!

---

### Day 0 – Arrival & Settling In  
| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Arrive at Charles de Gaulle / Orly → take RER B or airport shuttle to your hotel. Check‑in; drop bags. |
| **Afternoon** | Light walk around your neighborhood (e.g., Marais, Latin Quarter) to get bearings. Grab a croissant from a boulangerie nearby. |
| **Evening** | Dinner at a classic bistro (suggestion: **Le Coupe Chou**, near Saint‑Germain). Try coq au vin or duck confit. |

*Tip*: Get a **Navigo Week Pass** (€22.80) for unlimited metro/bus rides during your stay.

---

### Day 1 – Classic Landmarks  
| Morning | Visit Notre-Dame Cathedral & Sainte-Chapelle (both inside the Île de la Cité). |
|---------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| Lunch   | Picnic along the Seine (buy baguette, cheese, charcuterie). |
| Afternoon | Walk across Pont Neuf → explore Palais des Tuileries → visit Musée du Luxembourg (if interested in contemporary works). |
| Evening | Sunset view from the Eiffel Tower’s second floor (book tickets online ahead). Dine at **58 Tour Eiffel** or enjoy street-side crepes. |

---

### Day 2 – Art & Culture  
| Morning | Louvre Museum (arrive early, skip-the-line ticket). Focus on Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, Egyptian antiquities. |
| Lunch   | Café Marly within the Louvre courtyard. |
| Afternoon | Stroll through Jardin des Tuileries → head to Place Vendôme → shop window‑shopping. |
| Evening | Attend a classical concert at Théâtre des Champs‑Élysées or catch a jazz club in Le Marais. |

---

### Day 3 – Montmartre & Sacré-Cœur  
| Morning | Tram #12 to Montmartre. Explore artists’ square (Place du Tertre), climb up to Basilique du Sacré‑Cœur for panoramic city views. |
| Lunch   | Traditional French lunch at **La Maison Rose** or try falafel on Rue des Abbesses. |
| Afternoon | Wander down Rue Lepic → stop at Moulin Rouge entrance (even if no show). |
| Evening | Optional cabaret performance at Moulin Rouge (reserve seats). If you prefer something quieter, dine at **Le Consulat**. |

---

### Day 4 – Modern & Shopping  
| Morning | Centre Pompidou (modern art museum). Take photos of its colorful exterior. |
| Lunch   | Eat at **L'Avant-Garde** inside the building or grab a sandwich at a nearby café. |
| Afternoon | Head to Galeries Lafayette on Boulevard Haussmann. Don’t miss the rooftop terrace for sunset shots. |
| Evening | Relax at a wine bar such as **Ô Chateau** or have dinner at **Bistrot Paul Bert** (classic steakhouse). |

---

### Day 5 – Palace of Versailles (Optional Excursion)  
| Early Morning | Depart via RER C train (~45 min). Book a guided tour or self‑guided audio guide. |
| Midday | Explore Hall of Mirrors, Royal Apartments, Gardens (treat yourself to a picnic there!). |
| Late Afternoon | Return to Paris. Rest at your hotel. |
| Night | Casual dinner near your hotel or try a new cuisine (Japanese ramen, Moroccan tagine). |

*(If Versailles feels too long, swap this day for a relaxed Seine river cruise.)*

---

### Day 6 – Hidden Gems & Leisure  
| Morning | Canal Saint-Martin area: boutique shops, vintage stores, cafés. Great spot for Instagram pics. |
| Lunch | Brunch at **Holybelly** or **Café Charlot**. |
| Afternoon | Visit Musée d’Orsay (impressionism masterpieces). Then wander through the charming streets of Saint-Germain-des-Prés. |
| Evening | Farewell dinner at **Septime** (reservations required) or a cozy restaurant in the Latin Quarter. End with dessert at **Berthillon** ice cream on Ile Saint-Louis. |

---

### Day 7 – Departure Prep & Last‑Minute Souvenirs  
| Morning | Pack, check out, leave luggage at concierge. Quick last‑minute shopping at Marché aux Puces de Saint-Ouen (flea market). |
| Noon | Final meal: croque-monsieur at **Au Petit Plaisir**. |
| Afternoon | Retrieve luggage, head back to the airport using RER or taxi. |

---

## Practical Tips

| Category | Recommendation |
|----------|----------------|
| **Transport** | Navigo week pass covers all metros, buses, trams, RER lines (except high-speed trains). For short trips outside central zones, consider a single‑ride ticket or contactless payment. |
| **Dining** | Reserve tables two weeks before for popular spots. Use apps like LaFourchette or OpenTable. |
| **Language** | Basic phrases help: *Bonjour*, *Merci*, *Parlez-vous anglais ?*. Most Parisians speak English in tourist areas. |
| **Safety** | Keep valuables secure; pickpocketing common in crowded places. Avoid empty metro cars late at night. |
| **Packing List** | Comfortable walking shoes, light jacket (weather varies), power adapter (Type E/F), reusable water bottle, small umbrella, camera or smartphone with good photo app. |
| **Cash vs Card** | Credit cards accepted everywhere except some markets; keep ~50 EUR cash for small vendors. |
| **Health** | Bring prescription meds, basic first aid kit. France has excellent pharmacies. |

---

## Suggested Booking Platforms

| Service | Link |
|--------|-------|
| Flights | Skyscanner, Google Flights |
| Hotels | Booking.com, Airbnb, HotelTonight |
| Museums/Tickets | official museum websites, Tiqets, GetYourGuide |
| Restaurants | LaFourchette, OpenTable |
| Tours | Viator, LocalGuides, CityPass Paris |

---

### Next Steps?

1. **Confirm Dates:** Let me know exact arrival/departure times so I can adjust flight recommendations.  
2. **Budget Details:** Do you prefer luxury hotels ($300+/night) or mid-range accommodations ($120–$180)?  
3. **Special Requests:** Any dietary restrictions, accessibility needs, or specific experiences you'd love to add?  

Once I have those details, I can fine‑tail everything—from flight itineraries to daily reservations—and even generate a printable PDF agenda!
